initial_plan.can_answer_question: partly: crash data has no miles-driven exposure denominator, so it cannot measure deaths per mile; it can show annual counts of crashes with at least one motorist death
initial_plan.metric: annual count of crash rows where number_of_motorist_killed is greater than zero
initial_plan.denominator: none; an annual crash count, not a rate
initial_plan.population: police-reported NYC crash rows dated from 2013 through 2025 inclusive

data_check_interpretation.findings: The baseline planned period contains 2,132,218 crash rows; every year from 2013 through 2025 has records spanning January 1 through December 31. There are no NULL crash dates in the file, and no missing or negative number_of_motorist_killed values on the planned rows. The file extends from 2012-07-01 to 2026-06-11, so the later partial 2026 coverage is outside the plan.
data_check_interpretation.row_decisions: Keep the planned-year records with known nonnegative motorist-death counts; there are no such rows to exclude for missing/impossible counts. For the metric, count only rows with at least one recorded motorist death, and do not give multiple-death crashes extra weight. No miles-driven exposure rows exist in this dataset.

final_plan.can_answer_question: partly: cannot answer whether the risk per mile declined because the dataset contains no miles-driven exposure; it can describe annual counts of crashes with motorist deaths
final_plan.metric: annual count of crash rows where number_of_motorist_killed is greater than zero; each qualifying crash row counts once
final_plan.denominator: none; annual count of qualifying crash rows
final_plan.population: police-reported NYC crash rows with a known, nonnegative number_of_motorist_killed and crash_date in calendar years 2013–2025 inclusive
final_plan.limitations: The crash file has no miles driven, so crash counts do not measure per-mile risk. This metric counts a crash once regardless of how many motorists died in it. Data checks found 0 missing or negative motorist-death counts among 2,132,218 planned-year rows and no missing crash dates; each planned year spans the full calendar year.
